newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse sees Q3 1997 derivatives launch.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse sees Q3 1997 derivatives launch.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange postponed the launch of derivatives trade to the third quarter of 1997 from the second quarter, the bourse's deputy president Wlodzimierz Magiera said on Wednesday.
"We want to trade derivatives this year...beginning with futures contracts on the WIG-20 index in the third quarter," Magiera said at a ceremony of the bourse's 1,000th session.
He said the bourse still had legal, technical and organisational problems to solve before the launch.
Magiera also said National Investments Funds (NFIs) may start trade on the bourse in the third quarter instead of the earlier planned launch in the first half of this year.
All 15 NFIs in Poland's mass privatisation programme have already completed their issue prospectuses, bringing them closer to the planned flotation.
Magiera said other Polish institutions, such as the over-the-counter electronic broker SPOiF SA and the Warsaw Commodities Exchange, were also interested in setting up derivatives trade.
